contracts.selectedText:
**F-S01 — Source boundary.** Follow L-F01–L-F07 and F-P01–F-P06. The exact source root is the existing computer-system-engine package, bound by the generation inventory. Create only `src/journal/filesystem/source-owner.mjs` and `src/journal/diagnostics.mjs`; edit only `package.json` to add `./journal/filesystem/source-owner` and `./journal/diagnostics` exports to those paths. Preserve all existing package fields and exports. No dependency additions, operational data writes by the generator, new framework, alternate codec, permanent index, sidecar authority or Code-to-System import. The inventory binds the package bytes and absent targets before invocation. Read-only source inputs provide existing laws, not authority to preserve old storage machinery.


**F-S03 — Host and kernel protection.** Require an explicit absolute existing nonsymlink directory and verify every component of its resolved path with lstat/descriptor identity. Reject non-Linux execution and a journal-root statfs type other than the locally assessed `0xef53` before source mutation. The host profile alone does not override those checks. Validate closed configuration and exact bounded canonical UTF-8 host bytes as L-H01/L-H05 require. Treat a missing configuration as unavailable at runtime; never initialize from openSourceOwner.

Open the stable maintenance.lock using O_RDWR, O_CREAT and O_NOFOLLOW, mode 0600; verify it is a regular file at the bound root. Invoke `/usr/bin/flock --exclusive --nonblock 3` synchronously with that descriptor supplied as child fd 3, ignored input/output and captured bounded stderr, and a finite ten-second helper timeout. Exit 1 means maintenance-busy; unavailable/unsupported locking means storage-unsupported; other host failures are storage-unavailable. The parent retains its open descriptor for the full operation. Do not unlink the lock. Coordinate reentry across owner objects with a process-local registry keyed by physical device/inode, plus the kernel gate for other processes and duplicate module instances. Registry membership is host-internal state, never a request-supplied key or substitute for flock.

Bind root, lock and host identity/content at construction under the gate; acquire the gate and revalidate them before every callback and before its result escapes. A changed host/root/lock invalidates the owner rather than silently rebinding. A live scope is privately branded and checked at every method entry, expires in finally before descriptor release, and cannot support deferred thenables. Reject reentry as maintenance-busy. If no publication may have occurred, a callback's own thrown value escapes unchanged after release; actual host failures are translated at the operation which observed them. Once publication might be visible, a later failing acknowledgment/final identity check takes publication-uncertain precedence.


**F-S08 — Independent receiving responsibility.** The source provider returns a candidate from this public contract and exact supplied bytes, with no tool access and no private receiving material. It is not asked to execute or certify future acceptance. Refuse only for a specific missing/contradictory source requirement or inability to supply the implementation, not because the intentionally isolated provider cannot run the assessor. The independent operator commits private fixtures before generation, materializes the closed patchset, syntax-checks the staged files and runs it in a network-denied namespace with only required dependencies and fixture directories. No credentials or operational corpus enter receiving. Review source for binding/descriptor cleanup, budget enforcement, gate lifetime, private diagnostic leakage, uncertainty handling and custody correspondence even if fixtures pass. No assessor behavioral repair or private-feedback retry is permitted.

Receiving must demonstrate initialization/retry/conflict, unchanged identities across reopen, same-process and separate-process exclusion, scope expiry and callback error preservation, ordinary/unique shared discovery, original command-payload recovery, duplicate/conflicting requests, pending-to-admitted recovery, retained blocks, membership-only additions, exact selections and accounting, source withdrawal/corruption, changed root/host/lock refusal, configured resource refusals and actual required-source synchronization with failure injection. Further integration receiving must establish all L-O06 consumer effects and legacy retirement before the replacement is called complete. A finite fixture set alone does not prove all host/production properties.


**F-S09 — Evidence and promotion boundary.** Record the exact specification/dependency/input/assay/candidate digests, requested and observed Luna model, executable/profile, namespace observation, invocation duration, measured tokens, and cash cost unavailable when not reported. The generation inventory and public source bundle are immutable during an invocation. Any unexpected provider tool activity or source change rejects it. A passing owner candidate remains a dependency, not an accepted operating application. Before any promotion recheck all protected bytes and absent targets and preserve exact originals; report partial multi-file promotion honestly. Do not remove the old writer or mutate a real journal in this dependency order. The connected facade/domain/consumer and offline migration patchset carries the retirement obligation.


**F-S11 — Two dependent source-generation stages.** The complete owner may be generated in two source calls after the first whole-owner provider declined to supply an implementation. This changes the source-call boundary, not the required final behavior, private receiving fixtures, source inventory or promotion condition. Both stages remain unaccepted outside the working repository until the combined result satisfies the complete order. The operator does not write or repair product behavior.

Stage A supplies the complete diagnostics module, package exports, explicit host initialization, immutable root/host binding, descriptor-owned gate and withOperation lifetime/error handling. Within source-owner.mjs it leaves exactly one designated private generation seam:

```js
function createSourceScope(operation) {
  throw new TypeError("journal source view fabrication incomplete");
}
```

This seam is an explicit staging-only incompleteness marker, never a runtime fallback and never promotable. withOperation calls it under the held gate before invoking the trusted callback. Its operation argument is a frozen private object containing exactly root (bound absolute directory), configuration (the deeply frozen admitted host configuration), cache (one owner-private mutable cell with property value, initially undefined), assertLive (throws outside this operation), assertBindings (rechecks current root/host/lock bindings), and markPublicationPossible (sets the operation's uncertainty flag irreversibly). Methods check the captured lifetime, not a caller-supplied flag. The argument is never returned or serialized. The host stage provides all actual initialization and host-boundary behavior; it does not pretend a source view exists.

Stage B receives the exact generated Stage-A bytes and the source-view specification/dependencies. It replaces that private seam with the complete source reader, scope methods, source-derived cache, publication and durability behavior; additional private helpers may be inserted within the same owner module. It may refine Stage-A private helper composition where necessary while preserving all host and diagnostic contracts. It removes the staging-only error and all placeholders. No public alternate constructor or partially functional scope survives. The final inventory retains the original checkout package digest and absent creation targets for eventual promotion; Stage-B staging edits are bound separately to the precise Stage-A source bytes.

Syntax and public source review may occur between stages; the complete committed private receiver runs only against the composed result after Stage B. Source-provider input includes only the clauses and dependency source needed for its stage, with hashes binding the full order and predecessor files. Private receiving outcomes are never sent to either provider. A refusal or failure preserves the incomplete stages as unaccepted evidence and does not authorize hand completion or a reduced acceptance claim.


**F-S13 — Stage-B completion includes remaining public host defects.** Revised Stage A attempt03 is a staged, syntactically valid but unaccepted precursor. Its cache and initial lock binding are now retained, and its imports resolve to the declared modules. Public review still finds the following host-contract failures; Stage B must correct them while completing the source view. No private receiving has run:

- parseHost compares two normalized canonical strings, not exact source bytes. Compare the bounded bytes read from the descriptor to the exact canonical host text plus one LF. Refuse leading/trailing whitespace, duplicate keys, a missing LF or multiple LFs. Shared strict admission may normalize input; normalization alone is not canonical-source correspondence.
- verifyUniqueCustody duplicates the slot hash law, accepts noncanonical record bytes, omits aggregate source-byte accounting, allocates from an opened size without bounding that current size, and performs one read which can be short. Use parseUniqueJournalRecord with the filename's exact slot digest; never reconstruct the slot algorithm in Systems. Require exact canonical verified record plus LF. Bound the opened descriptor size before allocation and use a bounded read loop with one excess-detection byte, verify before/after named and descriptor identity/size, charge overflow-safe total bytes and distinct physical-source counts, and bind every source parent. Apply the configured discovery-work limit to root/family/version entries as well as final filenames. Unexpected versions or identity-bearing custody may not be skipped. Oversize capacity is resource-limit, malformed data is source-corrupt, and actual I/O failure keeps its host diagnostic.
- Identical-existing initialization fsyncs the host and lock but omits directory ancestry and does not bind the synchronized host descriptor to the bytes it verified. Reuse the final private bound-descriptor barrier for both new and identical-existing initialization: verified exact host and stable lock plus directory ancestry through `/`, with final unchanged identities. Publication's helper barrier does not discharge lock/host verification. No EEXIST republishing or source creation is allowed for an identical-existing barrier.
- Several close/cleanup paths either swallow the only failure or replace an earlier failure. Capture a separate Boolean indicating a prior failure, because a callback may throw undefined. Preserve that thrown value when cleanup also fails. On otherwise successful work, translate the cleanup failure and apply publication-uncertain when publication may be visible; this includes release/close after initialization and after withOperation's callback returns. The uncertainty flag must remain available through release, not stop at the inner callback boundary. Do not return a successful result before mandatory cleanup has completed.
- Always revalidate the captured bindings before constructing an acknowledged result; a failed identity check invalidates the owner even when it occurs before the scope is built. Never reset a failed owner to a new root/host/lock. Recheck parent bindings immediately before opening or publishing under them. Use the same protected provenance for initialization, ordinary sources and closure barriers rather than adding a weaker initialization path.

These are required corrections to existing F-S03/F-S06/F-S07/F-S12, not new capabilities. Remove obsolete helper paths and unused constants as the source functions are composed. The private receiver remains byte-identical; its eventual result and source review determine acceptance of the complete owner, not this intermediate syntax check.


**F-S22 — Isolate existing-source synchronization from host repair.** Attempt21 supplied no B2b2 source. Generate B2b2a as the physical implementation of L-O28 and composition with the already reviewed requiredSourceClosure. It introduces a private reusable existing-file barrier and replaces requireDurableInScope; the two publication seams remain. This phase leaves all host initialization, gate, scanner and cleanup functions unchanged. B2b2b subsequently applies every F-S13 host correction using that same barrier, without claiming that B2b2a alone repairs the host or completes acceptance.

The private barrier accepts a bound absolute root, expected existing file descriptions and a caller-provided binding assertion. Descriptions identify root-relative nonsymlink regular files and their expected device/inode. Source and host descriptions also carry bounded exact previously verified bytes/digest and length; a stable maintenance-lock description can supply its already held descriptor without inventing semantic content or transferring descriptor ownership. It checks each named binding, reads bounded bytes from the verified descriptor, requires exact previous bytes/digest, and synchronizes selected physical files once while preserving all selected aliases for final checks. It holds and verifies the relevant ancestor directory descriptors before opening under them, synchronizes unique directories bottom-up through `/`, and rechecks named/held identities and caller bindings before success. Never create, publish, replace or delete anything. Close every descriptor it owns; preserve any primary thrown value using a separate failure flag, and surface a lone cleanup failure through the closed host diagnostic. Caller-owned descriptors remain open. The publication-uncertainty precedence still belongs to the protected outer operation and is completed in B2b2b/B2c.

requireDurableInScope invokes requiredSourceClosure, obtains the exact selected records from the current private view, runs that existing-source barrier, and stores the successful journal/semantic-reference/physical-source evidence privately behind a frozen opaque scope-bound receipt. It rechecks the live scope/bindings before acknowledgment. No serializable durable flag or public receipt validator is added. The private plan is never returned as proof of synchronization. Full L-O28 coverage and immutable independent receiving remain required after composition.

For this focused generation, supply exact excerpts containing the existing imports, required private helper definitions and the requireDurableInScope target, plus all top-level declaration names to prevent collisions. Bind each excerpt to its full file digest, original byte position and exact text; verify its occurrence before generation. The complete source file and ordinary F-P inventory stay bound and protected, and the unchanged materializer still resolves replacements against the entire file. Omit unrelated read-only dependency source and unrelated host-repair clauses from this invocation. This projection reduces input volume; it grants no authority to rewrite omitted code, extend the writable inventory or relax acceptance.

## L-O01 — Constructor and synchronous operation scope

The internal constructor is `openSourceOwner(storeDirectory)`, where storeDirectory is the explicit absolute physical journal directory obtained through L-H02's existing path laws. It validates/binds the root and host configuration but never initializes an absent store. Public `openJournal(root)` continues to take a settlement root; no second journal-directory suffix is added. Separate standalone stores retain their own admitted host configuration. Multiple owner objects referring to the same physical store use the same kernel gate and cannot execute concurrently, even within one process.

The owner exposes only `withOperation(perform)` to trusted System composition. It acquires the L-S04 gate, verifies root/lock/host identities, discovers and refreshes the complete bounded source view, invokes `perform(scope)` synchronously, checks identities again, constructs the result and releases its descriptor in a finally path. No user or model supplies perform. Detect a Promise/thenable return and refuse; never allow asynchronous host mutation to outlive the gate. A callback exception does not imply rollback of an already published source. Publication-uncertain precedence applies once publication may have occurred. No exception path unlinks the lock.

A scope is privately branded, belongs to that owner and operation epoch, and expires before lock release. Every method checks that lifetime. Retained scope objects, callbacks attempting a public nested operation, cross-owner use and reconstructed JSON objects cannot acquire authority; reentrant public access returns maintenance-busy. Pure immutable results may survive the scope; source handles, descriptors and durability evidence do not become reusable grants. Domain validation inside an operation receives this same scope and must not call a facade that reacquires the gate.


## L-O14 — Facade folds preserve failure distinctions

The current scanCausalEvents catches both row decoding and the caller's fold in one catch, counting either failure as a malformed row. An isolated execution of the exact current function confirms a thrown application callback error becomes a successful-looking `{result:initial,rows:0,malformed:1}`. This is source migration evidence; it does not demonstrate a production occurrence.

In the replacement, verify the complete selected admitted source view before any fold callback, as L-O02 requires. Decode/classify each row separately from callback execution. A structurally valid non-row witness can contribute the documented non-row/malformed count without becoming an EAVT assertion. A recognized corrupt source or incomplete selected admission cannot be classified as an ignorable malformed row. Once a decoded row is passed to the caller, any callback-thrown value propagates unchanged; it must not increment malformed, return an empty result or appear to be a completed fold. Successful rows count completed callback applications. A thrown fold does not imply rollback of earlier in-memory accumulator mutations or published effects.

Apply the same distinction to feed, date, territory, subject and through-date folds, including trusted feed-selection predicates. Preserve their selected membership, causal ordering and result metadata while removing per-feed read-through authorities. Selection/fold callbacks remain synchronous and scoped; a thenable result refuses rather than escaping the protected operation. This does not make arbitrary callback code transactionally reversible or safe to run with broad host authority. Domain readers receive only the already admitted scope they need.

Receiving must show no callback runs on an incomplete selected feed, a valid decoded row reaches the callback exactly as before, a callback failure survives by identity/value, a genuine non-row witness is separately counted, and current work/authority readers cannot convert journal-unavailable into an empty successful history. The pure semantic-record resolver's separate exception-presence handling is the same required distinction, not a license to reuse application exception objects as an admission verdict.

## Necessary transformation

L-F02's exact-substring contract cannot create a System module or retire its superseded Code implementation. L-S06/L-S09 require both effects, including consumer migration. This order extends the deterministic materialization boundary for explicitly declared source creation and deletion. It does not add a scheduler, model harness, repository mutation service or product-code generator. Existing edit-only orders and their evidence remain unchanged. The source provider continues deriving behavioral source; the operator's deterministic materializer performs only declared byte transformations on a fresh staged directory.

**F-P01 — Opt-in input.** A patchset work order binds an exact source root and an input inventory. The inventory is a JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `sourceRoot`, `files`, `clauses`. Kind is `source-patchset-input`; version is integer 1. SourceRoot is an absolute existing directory. Files is a path-keyed object. Every key is an admitted relative POSIX source path: nonempty components, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, no dot/dot-dot component, absolute prefix, backslash or NUL. Each descriptor is exactly either `{state:"present",sha256}` or `{state:"absent"}`. Present entries bind lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes; absent entries authorize only creation. No path may be an ancestor of another admitted path. Clauses is a nonempty unique list of recognized nonempty clause-ID strings. Existing paths must be ordinary regular files and all existing ancestors, including the root's own path, must be nonsymlink directories; absent paths must also have no symlink or nondirectory ancestor. The inventory is trusted work-order input, not generated permission to touch files.

The concrete storage order must enumerate its exact writable files and clause IDs before source generation. This generic extension grants no writable source path by itself. Read-only dependencies and governing specification hashes remain protected under L-F01/L-F07 and are additional to this writable inventory.

**F-P02 — Closed candidate.** The new opt-in output is exactly `{kind:"source-patchset",version:1,disposition,reason,changes}`. Disposition is `candidate` or `refused`; reason is a string. A refusal has zero changes. A candidate has at least one change. Each admitted path occurs at most once, and every change contains a nonempty unique `clauses` array drawn from the inventory. No generated shell command, URL, dependency installation, permission change or recursive delete operation exists.

Changes are exactly one of:

- `{operation:"edit",path,inputSha256,replacements,clauses}` against a present entry. Each replacement is exactly `{before,after}`. Before is nonempty text occurring exactly once when that replacement is applied; after is text. Apply replacements in order against the original bound UTF-8 text. The one input digest remains the original file digest, not an intermediate value. The list is nonempty.
- `{operation:"create",path,text,clauses}` against an absent entry. Text is complete strict UTF-8 source, supplied by the generator; the operator must not fill behavioral placeholders. Creation emits an ordinary file with mode 0644. An executable entrypoint should normally be invoked through its existing runtime; changing execution bits requires a separately admitted order.
- `{operation:"delete",path,inputSha256,clauses}` against a present entry. This removes that exact file from the staged result. It does not delete directories, follow links, delete imports automatically or authorize removing unlisted data. Necessary consumer and export changes must appear as separately bound changes in the same work family.

All objects are closed. Reject Boolean values masquerading as integer versions, unknown operations, malformed digests, repeated paths, unknown clauses, invalid UTF-8, missing inputs, changed input bytes or an unexpectedly present creation target. Do not normalize generated paths or repair a refused candidate.

**F-P03 — Validate before staging.** The materializer rechecks every inventory entry, including unchanged inputs, before creating any staged output. It validates the whole candidate and calculates all intended output bytes in memory before writing. A malformed candidate therefore leaves no stage directory. It may inspect file metadata and bytes, but it never imports, evaluates or executes candidate text. The only mechanical transformations are the specified text replacements, creation and file omission.

Use a fresh nonexistent stage directory outside the source root. A stage ancestor cannot be a symlink or non-directory. The operator chooses that path; it is not accepted from the candidate. Copy each unchanged admitted present file and each resulting changed file into the stage at its declared relative path, preserving the existing file's permission bits for retained/edited files. Deleted inputs are omitted and their digests/modes retained in the receipt. Do not copy the repository's unbounded contents or leave links from the stage into the working checkout. Recheck all original inputs after staging before writing the staged result receipt. A concurrent change invalidates the stage and prevents acceptance; it does not authorize changing the concurrent work.

A host I/O error during staging may leave a partial staged directory. It must have no successful receipt; report failure and preserve it for inspection. Do not represent staging as an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction. A retry uses a fresh stage and fresh validation rather than overwriting an uncertain directory.

**F-P04 — Staged receipt and assessment.** The operator writes a sibling `<stage>.receipt.json` only after successful validation/staging/revalidation. The receipt contains kind `source-patchset-stage`, integer version 1, inventory/candidate digests, the materializer digest, each original path's presence/digest/mode, each final path's presence/digest/mode, and disposition `staged-unaccepted`. No receipt claims product acceptance or promotion. A receipt target already present refuses before staging; receipt creation is exclusive. A receipt write failure is a failed stage operation even if all source files have been written.

Independent assessment uses the exact staged tree plus explicitly admitted read-only dependencies. A retired file must be absent from that assessment namespace; a fallback mount of the old checkout must not make deleted code available again. Verify source creation, changed consumers and actual retired routes, not only that new files load. The private assessment remains excluded from source generation under L-F03–L-F05. Source provider and materializer receive no permission to amend acceptance fixtures after a failure.

**F-P05 — Promotion remains separate.** This materializer has no shared-checkout mutation or deployment mode. Product promotion remains governed by L-F07 plus the concrete work order's creation/deletion preconditions. Recheck all present/absent expectations before touching any target. Do not delete an obsolete file unless the complete affected capability and consumer migration have independently passed. A staged tree, deleted-path list or model assertion is insufficient. A multi-file promotion must record partial host failure accurately; it must not claim atomicity that the filesystem mechanism does not provide. Never restore over unrelated concurrent edits while trying to roll back a partial operation.

**F-P06 — Independent mechanical observations.** Demonstrate in disposable files that one batch creates a new file, changes an exact unique substring, retires a bound old file and carries an unchanged input, while leaving the source root byte-identical. Exercise stale/absent mismatch, ambiguous replacement, malformed/extra fields, repeated changes, unknown clause, path traversal, symlink input/ancestor, a path ancestor collision, malformed UTF-8 and an existing stage/receipt. Invalid input must produce no successful receipt or shared source mutation. The observations verify deterministic materialization only; they do not accept any journal or assistant behavior.

The initial realization may be a small operator-owned script retained with the fabrication evidence and invoked directly. It is not a new runtime package. This is mechanical tooling under the closed contract above; all product behavioral text in real candidates must still originate from the admitted isolated source-generation process.
